To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ring-shaped minipartides are a novel family of proteins that can be purified from the nucleoli of human cells.

ring shaped miniparticles are multisubunit protein complexes, comprised of at least 6 polypeptide chains, that can be reversibly disaggregated by EDTA, that contain no carbohydrate, that have an S20,w of 21S and that are immunologically similar across a number of human cells lines.
the miniparticles are a novel type of nuclear protein that are present in the nucleolus and the cytoplasm and are immunologically similar between different cell lines.

the purification and characterization of a new class of small ring-shaped minipartides found in the nucleus and cytoplasm.
a group of small ring-shaped proteins that have a wide tissue distribution and are found in both normal and malignant cells.
the purification and characterization of a class of ring-shaped minichromosome-like particles which are found in the nucleus and cytoplasm in a variety of normal human and malignant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ring miniparticles represent a class of proteins that are present in a wide variety of normal and transformed human and animal cell types and that have been purified to apparent homogeneity by a procedure involving several steps.
the miniparticles are a new class of nuclear proteins.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have purified a protein complex that is ubiquitous in the nucleus and cytoplasm and that is immunologically similar in many cell lines.

we have identified a novel class of ring shaped miniparticles which are present in the nucleus and cytoplasm, are not membrane associated, are comprised of at least 6 polypeptide chains, are immunologically similar and may represent a class of nuclear and cytoplasmic structural proteins.
we have purified a protein which is present in the nucleolus of a variety of cell types.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the miniparticles we have studied are not a unique feature of the nucleolus.

we now know that there is a class of small ring-shaped miniparticle in normal and transformed cells which is not a ribosomal particle, is not a membrane associated structure, and is immunologically similar in a variety of human cell lines.
these miniparticles are not unique to any one cell line and are not specific to any particular disease.
